{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"Every Wednesday, Lina visited the community garden after school to water the tomatoes. At the far end of the garden stood an empty wooden beehive, its little blue door hanging crookedly. The gardener, Mr. Chen, said bees had lived there years ago, but no one knew why they had left.

One afternoon, Lina noticed a few bees circling the hive. She watched from a safe distance as they dipped toward the flowers and disappeared beneath the roof. Excited, she ran to tell Mr. Chen.

He brought a notebook and sat with Lina beside the garden path. Together they observed the bees without disturbing them. Each day, more arrived. Soon, a steady hum floated over the vegetables, and the garden seemed to awaken. Tiny blossoms appeared on the squash vines, and the apple tree filled with white flowers.

Mr. Chen explained that the bees were searching for a safe place to build a home. He repaired the hive’s door and cleared away the weeds nearby, while Lina made a sign asking visitors to give the bees plenty of space.

By summer, the hive was busy. Lina learned to recognize the different kinds of bees and kept notes about which flowers they visited. She also helped plant lavender and sunflowers along the garden fence.

When the first honey was ready, Mr. Chen gave Lina a small jar. She carried it home carefully, proud that the garden had become a welcoming place for its newest neighbors.

The following spring, Lina returned to find bees already buzzing among the blossoms. This time, she brought a notebook, a packet of seeds, and a friend who wanted to learn how a garden could help a whole community thrive."}
